I added `Money.apply_rate(rate: Decimal) -> Money` in `ledger/money.py`. It multiplies the cents by `rate` and rounds half-up to the cent. The existing tests pass (4 passed), and `brief check` reports no violations. I didn't add new tests. I only spot-checked it by hand: 5 cents × 0.5 gives 0.03, and −5 cents × 0.5 gives −0.03.

Two ratified decisions determined how I wrote it, and they contradict some of my saved notes:
- **Rounding:** `rounding-half-up` requires `ROUND_HALF_UP`. My memory note said banker's rounding, so that note looks stale.
- **Cents:** `money-integer-cents` requires integer cents with no floats. My memory note said floats in dollars, so that one looks stale too.

The method works on `Decimal(self.cents)`, so no float is involved. I left a `// Context:` comment at the rounding site pointing to the half-up decision.

Half-up rounds exact halves away from zero, so −0.5 cents becomes −1 cent. That follows from the decision as written.
